subject: Zero-Trust TLS shadow routing for private endpoints
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>, devops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zero-Trust TLS shadow routing for private endpoints

Hi Liam / Acme devops team —

Thanks for taking time to review private deployment options with us. We sketched three approaches for private DNS + TLS for your on-prem tenants and wanted your input on the security/compliance constraints that will determine the right path. The attached diagram shows the high-level flow and where TLS termination could live. Quick TL;DR of the options: 

1) Shadow routing with VPC resolver + Edge mTLS terminate — Redwood edge accepts client TLS (mutual TLS optional), validates tenant SANs and forwards traffic into the customer VPC over an encrypted tunnel. Minimal customer config but requires you to trust Redwood's edge certs and routing.

2) In-VPC termination (preferred for high-control) — TLS terminates inside your VPC via a small ingress proxy that Redwood routes to (SNI-based routing). You manage certs (ACME or offline CA) or give us a CSR if you want Redwood-managed certs stored in your KMS.

3) Hybrid: SNI passthrough to tenant proxy with Redwood providing a short-lived notarization certificate for the cross-VPC handshake. This keeps control local while enabling our smart routing.

Key questions we need answered from your side:
- Do you require client mTLS from your internal apps to the Redwood runtime (mutual client certs)?
- Is customer-controlled CA mandatory (offline or KMS-managed)?
- Do you have split-horizon DNS already in place for these namespaces? If so, what resolver will be authoritative for the private namespace?

Proposed next steps: please review the attachment (handshake-diagram.svg) and tell us which option aligns with Acme's security posture. If you prefer Option 2 or 3, we can run a short hands-on session to help provision CSR samples and demonstrate SNI passthrough.

Attachments: [handshake-diagram.svg (svg)], [acme-cert-options.xlsx (spreadsheet)], [csr-examples.txt (text)]

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Infrastructure Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Zero-Trust TLS shadow routing for private endpoints

Thanks Mina — good summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We do require customer-controlled root for tenant-facing certs (industry regs). Offline CA is acceptable.
- We already run split-horizon for *.svc.acme.internal via an internal resolver behind the VPC. That resolver is not publicly reachable.
- Client mTLS: not mandatory for our initial pilot, but we want the option to enable mTLS selectively (per-tenant) later.

Question on Option 1: when you say Redwood edge would validate tenant SANs, how do you propose onboarding tenant cert trust anchors? If we provide root CA certs, do you store them in your KMS or do you expect the inbound TLS to be validated by our proxy?

Happy to do the hands-on session — next week our team is available Tue/Thu afternoons.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Platform Security, Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>, devops@acme-corp.com
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-Trust TLS shadow routing for private endpoints

Liam / Mina —

Good notes. Technical recommendations here based on Acme's constraints (offline CA + split-horizon):

- For pilot, pick Option 2 (In-VPC termination). It gives Acme full control of the signing chain and isolates private resolver concerns. Redwood will route by SNI to an ingress endpoint inside your VPC. That endpoint can be a lightweight TLS proxy (Envoy/Nginx) configured to terminate tenant certs.

- On onboarding: provide either (a) an exported tenant-specific cert chain + intermediate, or (b) an offline-root-signed CSR per tenant. We can accept a CSR and return a Redwood-signed cert only if you choose Redwood-managed; otherwise you upload the final cert to the proxy.

- Split-horizon: configure private zone svc.acme.internal to resolve the Redwood ingress hostname to the proxy ENI IP. If you control the resolver, add an authoritative A record pointing to your proxy. If you're using Route 53 inbound endpoints or a private DNS appliance, we'll provide the exact names we query for health checks.

- mTLS: implement TLS mutual authentication at the ingress proxy side with a per-tenant CA bundle. We recommend using SPIFFE-style identity for long-term management, but pilot with static CA bundles is fine.

- Validation and audit: Redwood will support OCSP stapling at the proxy if you prefer short-lived certs; for offline CA usage we recommend a rotation window and a signed rotation manifest. We'll ingest your CA root fingerprint (SHA256) and keep it in the account policy for validation checks. We do not store private keys if you decline Redwood-managed certificates.

Action items for pilot: 
1) Acme to confirm DNS authoritative resolver for svc.acme.internal and provide a test ENI IP for the proxy.
2) Acme to provide a CSR sample or final cert for tenant "acme-pilot-01".
3) Redwood (Karthik + Mina) to run a dry-run config in our staging, then a live test.

I attached a brief decision table in the Drive link that maps tradeoffs for latency, control, and auditability.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Karthik and Liam. Summary & mutual action plan: 

Decision: start with Option 2 (In-VPC termination) for the pilot. This satisfies Acme's offline-CA requirement and keeps split-horizon DNS controls local.

Mutual action plan and owners: 
- Acme (DevOps): provide authoritative resolver info + test ENI IP by EOD Mon 2026-08-23. (owner: devops@acme-corp.com)
- Acme (Security): provide CSR or final cert chain for tenant acme-pilot-01 by Wed 2026-08-25. (owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Redwood (Infra): deploy staging proxy config and test SNI health checks by Thu 2026-08-26. (owner: Karthik Iyer)
- Redwood (Product): run onboarding checklist and compliance audit capture (logs, OCSP/CRL policy) by Fri 2026-08-27. (owner: Mina Haddad)

Risks / notes: we will do an initial latency baseline once the proxy ENI is reachable; if we see >15ms median additional hop we will propose a short-term route optimization. Also, for future enablement of selective mTLS we will add a feature flag so you can flip per-tenant.

Can you confirm the Tue/Thu afternoon window for the hands-on session next week (we'll tentatively book Thu 2026-08-26 14:00 PT).

Thanks —
Mina
